# Wrenfield Archive Partnership

## 2026 Digitisation Programme — Delivery Plan and Budget

**Version:** 1.0 for the January 2026 Programme Board  
**Prepared by:** Programme Planner, Wrenfield Archive Partnership  
**Grant:** Heritage Digitisation Fund, £84,000  
**Programme period:** 1 January – 30 June 2026

---

## 1. Summary

The plan delivers **Collections A and B in full** and publishes both by **Friday 29 May 2026**, one month inside the grant deadline. Collection C is **not published in this phase**: the only written legal advice says the Harrow estate is unlikely to decide before autumn 2026, and a verbal “spring” assurance cannot satisfy a donor restriction that requires written permission.

The budget is **£84,000 exactly**: £79,780 committed and £4,220 (5.0%) held as contingency. The critical path is Collection A conservation, then A scanning, then A quality assurance and publication. Collection B runs on a separate Northgate track in March, after the A scanning block and before the summer humidity that defeated the 2024 nitrate pilot.

| Collection | Items | Controlling constraint | Delivery approach | Publish by | Direct cost |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| **A — Parish registers** | 1,800 bound volumes | 220 volumes (12.2%) need stabilisation first; book cradle required | Stabilise Jan–13 Feb; scan stable volumes first; 26 Bindwell days; complete scanning 6 Mar | **22 May 2026** | £27,200 |
| **B — Wrenfield Film Society** | 240 nitrate reels | Orphan works; cold storage; Filmtek only in the Northgate inspection room; 30-minute batch limit | Rights assessment Jan; Filmtek 9–20 Mar at 28 reels/day; QA and publish April | **30 Apr 2026** | £19,500 |
| **C — Harrow Estate papers** | 950 boxes | Donor restriction to 2030; written estate permission required; 8% mould-affected | No digitisation spend or publication in this phase; written permission pursued monthly | **Not in this phase** | £0 |

Direct costs above exclude the centrally held programme staff, shared data/publication costs and contingency. The full reconciliation is in section 6.

**Bottom line:** A and B are fully digitised and published by 29 May; the grant condition is met with a month of schedule float; C is a documented, deliberate exclusion rather than an unfunded aspiration.

---

## 2. Grant conditions and how the plan meets them

The conditions in `sources/brief.md` are mapped to delivery commitments below.

| Grant condition | How this plan meets it | Evidence at 30 June 2026 |

| At least two of the three priority collections fully digitised and published by 30 June 2026 | Collection A: all 1,800 volumes scanned, quality-assured and published by 22 May. Collection B: all 240 reels scanned, rights-assessed and published by 30 April. Internal deadline 29 May. | Scanning manifests, QA sign-off, live publication URLs, board completion certificate |
| Any orphan works must have a completed rights risk assessment before publication | Collection B assessment runs 12–30 January (15 staff days), producing a per-reel register. The register is cross-checked against the scanned reels during April QA; publication is signed off only when every reel has a completed record. | Per-reel rights register, rights officer sign-off, publication approval minute |
| Programme spend within £84,000; line-item budget required | Line-item budget totals £84,000, with £79,780 committed and £4,220 contingency. Monthly cashflow and forecast are reported to the board. | Finance ledger, monthly budget reports, final reconciliation |
| Nitrate film handling must follow the Partnership’s conservation policy | B is scanned only in the Northgate inspection room (16°C, 45% RH), which is inside Filmtek’s 15–20°C and 40–50% RH range. Reels return to the 4°C cold store after every batch. Batches stay within the policy limit of 40 reels and 30 minutes door-to-door, including scanning. | Batch log with timestamps, environmental logger data, conservator sign-off, encrypted-drive chain-of-custody records |
| Collection C donor restriction | No C publication and no C digitisation spend until written estate permission is received. Permission is requested in writing in January and followed up monthly. | Correspondence log; no C entries in the finance ledger |

---

## 3. The open questions: decisions and evidence

The three questions in `sources/open-questions.md` are answered from the programme pack. No sustained external research is needed: the pack contains the controlling site, vendor, rights and attendance records, and using an external source for the open-day figure or the Harrow permission would be less reliable than the Partnership’s own records. The only live confirmations are the Northgate site survey and the Filmtek booking, both scheduled as January delivery actions rather than desk research.

| Question | Decision | Basis | Effect on the plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Can Northgate support scanning the nitrate collection with the Filmtek scanner, and under what conditions? | **Yes — in the Northgate inspection room, not the cold store and not CRO.** | The inspection room is 16°C and 45% RH, inside Filmtek’s 15–20°C and 40–50% RH range. The cold store is 4°C and 35% RH, too cold and dry for the scanner. CRO is not certified for film and failed the 2024 pilot when humidity reached 62% and condensation appeared on 14 frames. | Filmtek is booked at Northgate for 9–20 March. The batch protocol in Appendix B applies. Digitised files travel to CRO on encrypted drives because Northgate has no network. |
| 2. How many people attended the 2025 open day, for the newsletter? | **2,340 visitors.** | `sources/prior-notes.md` records the 2025 open-day attendance as 2,340. This is the Partnership’s own recorded figure. | Use “2,340 visitors” in the June newsletter and the evaluation report. No further research is required. |
| 3. Will the Harrow estate give written permission for Collection C before 30 June 2026? | **Not reliably. Plan for no; treat any permission as upside.** | The estate’s solicitor wrote in August 2025 that a decision is unlikely before autumn 2026. The donor liaison officer recorded an uncorroborated verbal assurance in September 2025 that the estate “expects to resolve it by spring”. Written legal advice outweighs a verbal assurance, and the two are inconsistent. | Collection C is excluded from the delivery commitment and receives no digitisation spend. The written request is pursued monthly. If permission arrives, it requires a funder-approved variation; it does not displace A or B. |

### 3.1 Question 1 in detail — the Northgate conditions

The inspection room is the only compliant location in the Partnership’s estate for the Filmtek scanner:

- **Temperature and humidity:** 16°C and 45% RH are comfortably inside the scanner’s 15–20°C and 40–50% RH operating range. The room is adjacent to the cold store and connected by a pass-through hatch, so reels do not need outdoor acclimatisation.
- **Cold store:** 4°C and 35% RH. The scanner cannot operate there, and nitrate must return to cold storage whenever it is not being scanned.
- **CRO:** certified at 18–22°C and 40–55% RH for paper, but not certified for film. The 2024 pilot is decisive evidence against repeating nitrate work there: humidity reached 62% by the afternoon, condensation appeared on 14 frames, and the conservator stopped the run. The programme runs into summer, which makes CRO even less suitable.
- **Batch limit:** the conservation policy allows up to 40 reels to leave the cold store for at most 30 minutes, including scanning time. The 40-reel figure is an upper bound, not a target. The operative constraint is the 30-minute window. At an assumed average of about three minutes per reel at scan speed, a compliant batch is seven reels, giving four batches and 28 reels per day. This is the basis for the Filmtek booking, not a notional six batches of 40.
- **Conditions to confirm before installation:** power, floor loading, door widths and scanner footprint in the inspection room; logger alarms at 15°C and 20°C, and at 40% and 50% RH; a written abort procedure; and a conservator on call during the scanning fortnight.
- **Data transfer:** Northgate has no public network. Files are written to encrypted drives, checksummed, and carried to CRO the same day under a signed chain-of-custody form.

### 3.2 Question 2 in detail — the open-day figure

The 2025 open day drew **2,340 visitors**. This figure is already recorded in the Partnership’s programme notes and should be used as stated in the newsletter. It is not a figure that requires external checking, and the plan does not allocate staff time to re-research it.

### 3.3 Question 3 in detail — the Collection C decision

Collection C cannot be published without written permission from the Harrow estate. The evidence points in two directions:

- The estate’s solicitor wrote in **August 2025** that a decision is **unlikely before autumn 2026**.
- The donor liaison officer recorded a **verbal assurance in September 2025** that the estate “expects to resolve it by spring”.

A verbal assurance is not written permission, and it is contradicted by the solicitor’s written advice. The prudent planning assumption is that written permission will **not** arrive before 30 June 2026. Collection C is therefore excluded from the two-collection commitment. The Partnership will:

1. Send a written permission request in the first week of January, copied to the estate’s solicitor.
2. Follow up monthly and log every response.
3. Commit **no digitisation spend** to C in this grant period.
4. If written permission arrives unexpectedly, treat it as upside and seek a funder-approved variation. It will not be used to displace A or B, and 950 boxes could not be fully digitised in the remaining weeks in any case.

The 8% of C that is mould-affected (about 76 boxes) is a collections-care issue. It is flagged to the conservator and kept out of the digitisation workflow; handling mould-affected material without treatment would create a health and conservation risk.

---

## 4. Delivery strategy

### 4.1 Collection A — Parish registers (1,800 bound volumes)

**The constraint.** About 12% of the collection — 220 volumes, using the conservator’s estimate — has binding failure and needs stabilisation before scanning. The conservator estimates six weeks for 220 volumes. Scanning must use a book cradle, and spines must never be pressed.

**The approach.** Conservation starts on **Monday 5 January** and runs for 30 working days, finishing on **Friday 13 February**. The 1,580 volumes that do not need stabilisation are queued first, so scanning can start on **Monday 2 February** while conservation finishes the fragile 220. The conservator signs off each batch of stabilised volumes before it enters the scanning queue.

Bindwell is booked for **26 days** at CRO: 25 scanning days plus one setup/buffer day. At a planning rate of 75 volumes per day, 25 days give 1,875 volumes of capacity against 1,800 required — a 4.2% margin. The scanning block runs **2 February – 6 March**, with 20 days in February (1,500 volumes) and five days in March (375 volumes). Collection A scanning is complete by **Friday 6 March**.

Quality assurance and ingest run **23 March – 10 April**, at a planning rate of 120 volumes per day. The first publication tranche goes live on **30 April**, and the full collection is published by **Friday 22 May**.

**Why scan stable volumes first.** Waiting for all 220 volumes to be stabilised would consume six of the programme’s 26 weeks before a single image was captured. Stable-first sequencing keeps the scanner productive, protects the fragile volumes, and still leaves a month of publication float.

### 4.2 Collection B — Wrenfield Film Society (240 nitrate reels)

**The constraint.** Nitrate film must be cold-stored when not being scanned. The scanner can only operate in the Northgate inspection room, and reels can leave the cold store only in batches of up to 40 for at most 30 minutes, including scanning time. The collection is orphan works, so a documented rights risk assessment is required before publication.

**The approach.** The rights assessment runs **12–30 January** (15 staff days, the equivalent of three weeks), producing a per-reel register. The assessment has schedule float to **10 April** before the publication gate, so a slower search does not put the deadline at risk.

Filmtek is booked for the two-week minimum, **9–20 March**. Day one is installation and calibration; the remaining nine days are scanning. At four batches per day of seven reels, and 28 reels per day, nine days give **252 reels of capacity** against 240 required — a 5% margin. Each batch is timed door-to-door and returned to the cold store immediately after scanning. The environmental logger runs continuously, and the conservator can stop the run at any point.

Quality assurance and the per-reel rights cross-check run **13–24 April**. Collection B is published on **Thursday 30 April**, after the rights officer and programme manager sign off every reel.

**Why March, not summer.** The 2024 pilot failed in July at CRO when humidity reached 62%. Scheduling B in March, in the controlled Northgate inspection room, avoids both the summer risk and the CRO environmental failure. It also places B after the A scanning block, so the digital archivist and the in-kind imaging team are not split between CRO and Northgate.

### 4.3 Collection C — Harrow Estate papers (950 boxes)

Collection C is **not a delivery target** in this phase. The donor restriction requires written estate permission before any publication; the written legal advice says a decision is unlikely before autumn 2026. The collection is also large (950 boxes) and 8% mould-affected, so even a late permission could not produce a full digitisation by 30 June. No C digitisation spend is committed. The permission request is kept alive, and any written permission would be handled through a funder variation rather than by silently reallocating A or B resources.

### 4.4 Capacity assumptions

| Activity | Planning rate | Days | Capacity | Basis |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| A conservation | 7.3 volumes/day | 30 | 220 volumes | Six weeks for 220 volumes (condition.md) |
| A scanning | 75 volumes/day | 25 scanning + 1 setup/buffer | 1,875 volumes | Bindwell book cradle; stable-first queue |
| A QA and ingest | 120 volumes/day | 15 | 1,800 volumes | Sampling, fixity, metadata |
| B rights assessment | 16 reels/day | 15 | 240 reels | Three weeks of staff time; per-reel record |
| B scanning | 28 reels/day | 9 | 252 reels | Four batches of seven reels, 30 minutes each |
| B QA and rights cross-check | 24 reels/day | 10 | 240 reels | Full reel check and register match |

These are planning rates, not guarantees. The first week of each scanning block validates them; if throughput is lower, the contingency and the prioritisation rules in section 8 apply.

### 4.5 Quality and publication standard

- **Collection A:** 400 ppi, 24-bit colour TIFF masters; JPEG access copies; no OCR (the registers are handwritten); collection-level and item-level metadata derived from the scanning manifest.
- **Collection B:** 2K scan, 16-bit DPX or 10-bit ProRes masters; H.264 access copies; frame-level checks; audio captured where present.
- **All outputs:** SHA-256 checksums at capture, on transfer and before publication; 3-2-1 backup (master at CRO, encrypted drive copy, offline copy); persistent identifiers and stable URLs.
- **Publication:** CRO catalogue and publication server; clear rights statements; Collection B carries an orphan-works notice and a take-down contact; Collection A is marked public domain.
- **Accessibility:** catalogue descriptions and captions where feasible; alt text for representative images.

These are programme standards. They should be checked against the Partnership’s digital preservation policy before the first ingest.

## 5. Month-by-month schedule, January–June 2026

| Month | Collection A | Collection B | Collection C, rights and governance | Gate / milestone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **January** | Conservation starts **Mon 5 Jan** (20 of 30 days); triage all 1,800 volumes; stable-first queue; Bindwell contract; scanner setup plan. | Rights assessment **12–30 Jan** (15 days); reel inventory and condition check in the cold store; Northgate site survey; Filmtek booking; encrypted-drive test. | Written permission request to the Harrow estate; funder clarification of the rights-assessment wording; board baseline; monthly report. | **Fri 30 Jan — Gate 1:** rights assessment complete; conservation on track; Northgate and Filmtek readiness signed off; contracts in place. |
| **February** | Scanning **2–27 Feb** (20 days; 1,500 volumes); conservation completes **Fri 13 Feb**; the 220 stabilised volumes are released and queued. | Batch-protocol dry run; environmental baseline; scanner delivery and installation plan; rights-register QA. | No C spend; monthly permission follow-up; board review of A throughput. | **Fri 27 Feb — Gate 2:** 1,500 A volumes scanned; 220 volumes stabilised; Northgate dry run passed; Filmtek on track for 9 March. |
| **March** | Scanning **2–6 Mar** (5 days; 375 volumes of capacity); A scanning complete by **Fri 6 Mar**; QA and ingest start **23 Mar**. | Filmtek on site **9–20 Mar**; 240 reels scanned at 28/day; daily fixity and encrypted transfer; cold-store return after every batch. | Rights register cross-checked against scanned reels; C monthly letter; board review of nitrate batch logs. | **Fri 20 Mar — Gate 3:** all 240 reels scanned; environmental log compliant; A scanning complete; chain of custody complete. |
| **April** | QA and ingest **23 Mar – 10 Apr**; first publication tranche **30 Apr**. | QA and rights sign-off **13–24 Apr**; Collection B published **30 Apr**. | No C spend; board review of permission status; funder progress report. | **Thu 30 Apr — Gate 4:** B published; A QA complete; first A tranche live. |
| **May** | Full A publication **22 May**; final QA and fixity check. | Post-publication monitoring; take-down process; evaluation data. | Newsletter using the **2,340** visitor figure; funder report draft. | **Fri 29 May — Gate 5:** A and B fully digitised and published; internal deadline met. |
| **June** | No new scanning; fixity re-check; handover to collections team. | No new scanning; final rights and access review. | Final report, finance reconciliation, lessons learned; C status recorded. | **Tue 30 Jun — Gate 6:** grant condition evidenced; spend at or below £84,000; final report and reconciliation signed off for submission by 31 July. |

**Critical path:** A conservation (5 Jan – 13 Feb) → A scanning (2 Feb – 6 Mar) → A QA (23 Mar – 10 Apr) → A publication (30 Apr / 22 May). Collection B is a parallel track: rights assessment (12–30 Jan) → Filmtek (9–20 Mar) → QA (13–24 Apr) → publication (30 Apr). The two scanning blocks do not overlap, which is deliberate: the digital archivist and the in-kind imaging team can concentrate on one site at a time, and nitrate work needs uninterrupted environmental attention.

**Schedule float:** both collections are published by 29 May, leaving June for compliance evidence, final reporting and any repair work. The internal deadline is the risk control, not the grant deadline.

### 6.3 Budget notes and assumptions

- **Filmtek booking:** the two-week minimum is treated as 10 working days, not 14 calendar days. Day one is installation and calibration; nine days are scanning. This is the single most important commercial assumption to confirm before the purchase order.
- **Bindwell:** 26 days at the quoted day rate. The scanner is on site from 1 February; the contract must reserve the two blocks around the Filmtek fortnight.
- **Conservation:** the rate includes labour and stabilisation materials. If the conservator finds more than 220 volumes needing work, additional days come from contingency and the queue is re-prioritised; the 1,580 stable volumes are not held up.
- **Rights assessment:** 15 staff days is the whole-collection estimate, with a documented record for each of the 240 reels. It is not 15 days per reel; that reading would require 720 weeks and is not a deliverable within any realistic grant.
- **Staff:** the grant-funded team is coordination, supervision, QA and publication. The Partnership provides imaging technicians, the CRO imaging suite, the Northgate cold store and inspection room, the publication server, finance and HR support in kind. Routine QA is carried out by the in-kind imaging technicians; the Digital Archivist samples and signs off. These in-kind contributions are not valued in the £84,000 and should be recorded as match funding if the application requires it.
- **VAT:** the budget assumes vendor rates are inclusive of VAT or that VAT is recoverable. Finance should confirm the treatment before contracts are signed. An irrecoverable VAT liability would exceed the contingency and would require a budget revision before commitment.
- **No Collection C costs:** there is no C digitisation, treatment or publication line. This is deliberate and is the main reason the A+B programme fits comfortably within the grant.

### 6.4 Contingency and change control

The £4,220 contingency is 5.0% of the grant. It is held centrally and released only by the Programme Board, in this order of priority:

1. Additional Filmtek days if nitrate throughput falls below 28 reels/day.
2. Additional conservation days if more than 220 A volumes need stabilisation.
3. Additional Bindwell days if A throughput falls below 75 volumes/day.
4. Additional QA/publication days if ingest slips.

It is **not** available for Collection C. Any C work would require written permission and a funder-approved variation, not a quiet reallocation.

Any change over £1,000 or five working days requires a written change request and board approval. Any change to the grant-funded scope requires funder approval.

### 6.5 Value for money

- **Bindwell versus MobileScan:** for 26 days, Bindwell costs £18,200. MobileScan would cost £24,700 in day rates plus £2,700 in item charges for 1,800 volumes — £27,400 — and it handles paper only, not bound volumes. Bindwell is both cheaper and technically required for the book cradle.
- **Filmtek:** the two-week minimum is the only nitrate-capable option in the pack. The plan uses 252 reels of capacity for 240 reels, a 5% margin, rather than paying for a third week.
- **Conservation:** stabilising 220 volumes prevents damage to fragile bindings and avoids re-scanning or conservation treatment after the programme. It is 10.7% of the budget and protects 100% of Collection A.
- **Rights assessment:** at 4.6% of the budget, it unlocks publication of all 240 reels and is a grant condition. Without it, Collection B cannot be published at all.
- **Contingency:** 5.0% is deliberately modest but sufficient to cover the most likely overruns — a few extra scanner days or conservation days. It is cheaper than over-booking vendors in the baseline.

## 7. Why this plan: decision log

| # | Decision | Rationale | Trade-off accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Deliver A and B in full; do not commit to C.** | C’s written permission is unlikely before autumn 2026, and 950 boxes plus mould treatment cannot be delivered in the remaining weeks. A and B are the only pair that can satisfy the two-collection condition. | C remains undigitised in this phase. The permission request is kept alive, and any permission becomes a future project or a funder variation. |
| 2 | **Scan B at the Northgate inspection room, not CRO.** | 16°C and 45% RH are inside Filmtek’s operating range; the cold store is 4°C; CRO is not certified for film and failed the 2024 pilot at 62% RH. | No network at Northgate, so encrypted drives and a daily courier; strict 30-minute batch discipline. |
| 3 | **Schedule B for 9–20 March, after A scanning.** | Avoids summer humidity; allows the rights assessment and site preparation to finish; prevents the small delivery team being split between CRO and Northgate. | A must be finished by 6 March. | 6 | **Book Filmtek for the two-week minimum and plan 28 reels/day.** | The 30-minute window, not the 40-reel cap, is the binding constraint. Four batches of seven reels give 28/day and 252 reels of capacity over nine scanning days. | Little slack for unusually long reels; a commissioning test and contingency days are essential. |
| 7 | **Complete the B rights assessment before publication, with a per-reel register.** | It is a grant condition. ## Appendix B — Nitrate batch protocol

1. **Before the batch:** check the inspection room is within 15–20°C and 40–50% RH; record the reading; confirm the scanner is calibrated; prepare a batch list of no more than 40 reels — in practice seven.
2. **Retrieve:** move the batch through the pass-through hatch from the cold store. Start the timer when the first reel leaves the cold store.
3. **Scan:** scan the batch. The clock includes scanning time, not just handling. Target 25 minutes to leave a five-minute margin.
4. **Return:** return every reel to the cold store through the hatch. Stop the timer and record the door-to-door time. The hard limit is 30 minutes.
5. **Abort:** if temperature or humidity goes outside range, or condensation appears on any reel, stop immediately, return the batch to the cold store, quarantine the affected reels and notify the Conservator.
6. **Data:** write files to an encrypted drive, generate SHA-256 checksums, complete the chain-of-custody form and transfer to CRO the same day.
7. **Log:** record batch number, reel IDs, start and end times, environmental readings, scanner operator, conservator sign-off and any incident.

## Appendix C — Collection B rights assessment checklist

For every reel, record:

- Reel identifier, title or working title, date, maker and provenance.
- Rights holders identified and the sources searched (Film Society minutes, donor records, local press, Companies House, the IPO orphan works register, and any other reasonable source).
- Search date, searcher and findings.
- Risk rating and the proposed publication decision (publish, publish with notice, restrict).
- Reviewer sign-off and date.
- Any take-down or contact information.

# Wrenfield Archive Partnership

## 2026 Digitisation Programme — Delivery Plan and Budget

**Version:** 1.0 for the January 2026 Programme Board  
**Prepared by:** Programme Planner, Wrenfield Archive Partnership  
**Grant:** Heritage Digitisation Fund, £84,000  
**Programme period:** 1 January – 30 June 2026

---

## 1. Summary

The plan delivers **Collections A and B in full** and publishes both by **Friday 29 May 2026**, one month inside the grant deadline. Collection C is **not published in this phase**: the only written legal advice says the Harrow estate is unlikely to decide before autumn 2026, and a verbal “spring” assurance cannot satisfy a donor restriction that requires written permission.

The budget is **£84,000 exactly**: £79,780 committed and £4,220 (5.0%) held as contingency. The critical path is Collection A conservation, then A scanning, then A quality assurance and publication. Collection B runs on a separate Northgate track in March, after the A scanning block and before the summer humidity that defeated the 2024 nitrate pilot.

| Collection | Items | Controlling constraint | Delivery approach | Publish by | Direct cost |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| **A — Parish registers** | 1,800 bound volumes | 220 volumes (12.2%) need stabilisation first; book cradle required | Stabilise Jan–13 Feb; scan stable volumes first; 26 Bindwell days; complete scanning 6 Mar | **22 May 2026** | £27,200 |
| **B — Wrenfield Film Society** | 240 nitrate reels | Orphan works; cold storage; Filmtek only in the Northgate inspection room; 30-minute batch limit | Rights assessment Jan; Filmtek 9–20 Mar at 28 reels/day; QA and publish April | **30 Apr 2026** | £19,500 |
| **C — Harrow Estate papers** | 950 boxes | Donor restriction to 2030; written estate permission required; 8% mould-affected | No digitisation spend or publication in this phase; written permission pursued monthly | **Not in this phase** | £0 |

Direct costs above exclude the centrally held programme staff, shared data/publication costs and contingency. The full reconciliation is in section 6.

**Bottom line:** A and B are fully digitised and published by 29 May; the grant condition is met with a month of schedule float; C is a documented, deliberate exclusion rather than an unfunded aspiration.

---

## 2. Grant conditions and how the plan meets them

| Grant condition | How this plan meets it | Evidence at 30 June 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| At least two of the three priority collections fully digitised and published by 30 June 2026 | Collection A: all 1,800 volumes scanned, quality-assured and published by 22 May. Collection B: all 240 reels scanned, rights-assessed and published by 30 April. Internal deadline 29 May. | Scanning manifests, QA sign-off, live publication URLs, board completion certificate |
| Any orphan works must have a completed rights risk assessment before publication | Collection B assessment runs 12–30 January (15 staff days), producing a per-reel register. The register is cross-checked against the scanned reels during April QA; publication is signed off only when every reel has a completed record. | Per-reel rights register, rights officer sign-off, publication approval minute |
| Programme spend within £84,000; line-item budget required | Line-item budget totals £84,000, with £79,780 committed and £4,220 contingency. Monthly cashflow and forecast are reported to the board. | Finance ledger, monthly budget reports, final reconciliation |
| Nitrate film handling must follow the Partnership’s conservation policy | B is scanned only in the Northgate inspection room (16°C, 45% RH), which is inside Filmtek’s 15–20°C and 40–50% RH range. Reels return to the 4°C cold store after every batch. Batches stay within the policy limit of 40 reels and 30 minutes door-to-door, including scanning. | Batch log with timestamps, environmental logger data, conservator sign-off, encrypted-drive chain-of-custody records |
| Collection C donor restriction | No C publication and no C digitisation spend until written estate permission is received. Permission is requested in writing in January and followed up monthly. | Correspondence log; no C entries in the finance ledger |

---

## 3. The open questions: decisions and evidence

The three questions in `sources/open-questions.md` are answered from the programme pack. No external verification is needed: the pack contains the controlling site, vendor, rights and attendance records. Using an external source for the open-day figure or the Harrow permission would be less reliable than the Partnership’s own records.

| Question | Decision | Basis | Effect on the plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Can Northgate support scanning the nitrate collection with the Filmtek scanner, and under what conditions? | **Yes — in the Northgate inspection room, not the cold store and not CRO.** | The inspection room is 16°C and 45% RH, inside Filmtek’s 15–20°C and 40–50% RH range. The cold store is 4°C and 35% RH, too cold and dry for the scanner. CRO is not certified for film and failed the 2024 pilot when humidity reached 62% and condensation appeared on 14 frames. | Filmtek is booked at Northgate for 9–20 March. The batch protocol in Appendix B applies. Digitised files travel to CRO on encrypted drives because Northgate has no network. |
| 2. How many people attended the 2025 open day, for the newsletter? | **2,340 visitors.** | `sources/prior-notes.md` records the 2025 open-day attendance as 2,340. This is the Partnership’s own recorded figure. | Use “2,340 visitors” in the June newsletter and the evaluation report. No further research is required. |
| 3. Will the Harrow estate give written permission for Collection C before 30 June 2026? | **Not reliably. Plan for no; treat any permission as upside.** | The estate’s solicitor wrote in August 2025 that a decision is unlikely before autumn 2026. The donor liaison officer recorded an uncorroborated verbal assurance in September 2025 that the estate “expects to resolve it by spring”. Written legal advice outweighs a verbal assurance, and the two are inconsistent. | Collection C is excluded from the delivery commitment and receives no digitisation spend. The written request is pursued monthly. If permission arrives, it requires a funder-approved variation; it does not displace A or B. |

### 3.1 Question 1 in detail — the Northgate conditions

The inspection room is the only compliant location in the Partnership’s estate for the Filmtek scanner:

- **Temperature and humidity:** 16°C and 45% RH are comfortably inside the scanner’s 15–20°C and 40–50% RH operating range. The room is adjacent to the cold store and connected by a pass-through hatch, so reels do not need outdoor acclimatisation.
- **Cold store:** 4°C and 35% RH. The scanner cannot operate there, and nitrate must return to cold storage whenever it is not being scanned.
- **CRO:** certified at 18–22°C and 40–55% RH for paper, but not certified for film. The 2024 pilot is decisive evidence against repeating nitrate work there: humidity reached 62% by the afternoon, condensation appeared on 14 frames, and the conservator stopped the run. The programme runs into summer, which makes CRO even less suitable.
- **Batch limit:** the conservation policy allows up to 40 reels to leave the cold store for at most 30 minutes, including scanning time. The 40-reel figure is an upper bound, not a target. The operative constraint is the 30-minute window. At an assumed average of about three minutes per reel at scan speed, a compliant batch is seven reels, giving four batches and 28 reels per day. This is the basis for the Filmtek booking, not a notional six batches of 40.
- **Conditions to confirm before installation:** power, floor loading, door widths and scanner footprint in the inspection room; logger alarms at 15°C and 50% RH; a written abort procedure; and a conservator on call during the scanning fortnight.
- **Data transfer:** Northgate has no public network. Files are written to encrypted drives, checksummed, and carried to CRO the same day under a signed chain-of-custody form.

### 3.2 Question 2 in detail — the open-day figure

The 2025 open day drew **2,340 visitors**. This figure is already recorded in the Partnership’s programme notes and should be used as stated in the newsletter. It is not a figure that requires external checking, and the plan does not allocate staff time to re-research it.

### 3.3 Question 3 in detail — the Collection C decision

Collection C cannot be published without written permission from the Harrow estate. The evidence points in two directions:

- The estate’s solicitor wrote in **August 2025** that a decision is **unlikely before autumn 2026**.
- The donor liaison officer recorded a **verbal assurance in September 2025** that the estate “expects to resolve it by spring”.

A verbal assurance is not written permission, and it is contradicted by the solicitor’s written advice. The prudent planning assumption is that written permission will **not** arrive before 30 June 2026. Collection C is therefore excluded from the two-collection commitment. The Partnership will:

1. Send a written permission request in the first week of January, copied to the estate’s solicitor.
2. Follow up monthly and log every response.
3. Commit **no digitisation spend** to C in this grant period.
4. If written permission arrives unexpectedly, treat it as upside and seek a funder-approved variation. It will not be used to displace A or B, and 950 boxes could not be fully digitised in the remaining weeks in any case.

The 8% of C that is mould-affected (about 76 boxes) is a collections-care issue. It is flagged to the conservator and kept out of the digitisation workflow; handling mould-affected material without treatment would create a health and conservation risk.

---

## 4. Delivery strategy

### 4.1 Collection A — Parish registers (1,800 bound volumes)

**The constraint.** About 12% of the collection — 220 volumes, using the conservator’s estimate — has binding failure and needs stabilisation before scanning. The conservator estimates six weeks for 220 volumes. Scanning must use a book cradle, and spines must never be pressed.

**The approach.** Conservation starts on **Monday 5 January** and runs for 30 working days, finishing on **Friday 13 February**. The 1,580 volumes that do not need stabilisation are queued first, so scanning can start on **Monday 2 February** while conservation finishes the fragile 220. The conservator signs off each batch of stabilised volumes before it enters the scanning queue.

Bindwell is booked for **26 days** at CRO: 25 scanning days plus one setup/buffer day. At a planning rate of 75 volumes per day, 25 days give 1,875 volumes of capacity against 1,800 required — a 4.2% margin. The scanning block runs **2 February – 6 March**, with 20 days in February (1,500 volumes) and five days in March (375 volumes). Collection A scanning is complete by **Friday 6 March**.

Quality assurance and ingest run **23 March – 10 April**, at a planning rate of 120 volumes per day. The first publication tranche goes live on **30 April**, and the full collection is published by **Friday 22 May**.

**Why scan stable volumes first.** Waiting for all 220 volumes to be stabilised would consume six of the programme’s 26 weeks before a single image was captured. Stable-first sequencing keeps the scanner productive, protects the fragile volumes, and still leaves a month of publication float.

### 4.2 Collection B — Wrenfield Film Society (240 nitrate reels)

**The constraint.** Nitrate film must be cold-stored when not being scanned. The scanner can only operate in the Northgate inspection room, and reels can leave the cold store only in batches of up to 40 for at most 30 minutes, including scanning time. The collection is orphan works, so a documented rights risk assessment is required before publication.

**The approach.** The rights assessment runs **12–30 January** (15 staff days, the equivalent of three weeks), producing a per-reel register. The assessment has schedule float to **10 April** before the publication gate, so a slower search does not put the deadline at risk.

Filmtek is booked for the two-week minimum, **9–20 March**. Day one is installation and calibration; the remaining nine days are scanning. At four batches per day of seven reels, and 28 reels per day, nine days give **252 reels of capacity** against 240 required — a 5% margin. Each batch is timed door-to-door and returned to the cold store immediately after scanning. The environmental logger runs continuously, and the conservator can stop the run at any point.

Quality assurance and the per-reel rights cross-check run **13–24 April**. Collection B is published on **Thursday 30 April**, after the rights officer and programme manager sign off every reel.

**Why March, not summer.** The 2024 pilot failed in July at CRO when humidity reached 62%. Scheduling B in March, in the controlled Northgate inspection room, avoids both the summer risk and the CRO environmental failure. It also places B after the A scanning block, so one digital archivist is not trying to supervise two sites at once.

### 4.3 Collection C — Harrow Estate papers (950 boxes)

Collection C is **not a delivery target** in this phase. The donor restriction requires written estate permission before any publication; the written legal advice says a decision is unlikely before autumn 2026. The collection is also large (950 boxes) and 8% mould-affected, so even a late permission could not produce a full digitisation by 30 June. No C digitisation spend is committed. The permission request is kept alive, and any written permission would be handled through a funder variation rather than by silently reallocating A or B resources.

### 4.4 Capacity assumptions

| Activity | Planning rate | Days | Capacity | Basis |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| A conservation | 7.3 volumes/day | 30 | 220 volumes | Six weeks for 220 volumes (condition.md) |
| A scanning | 75 volumes/day | 25 scanning + 1 setup/buffer | 1,875 volumes | Bindwell book cradle; stable-first queue |
| A QA and ingest | 120 volumes/day | 15 | 1,800 volumes | Sampling, fixity, metadata |
| B rights assessment | 16 reels/day | 15 | 240 reels | Three weeks of staff time; per-reel record |
| B scanning | 28 reels/day | 9 | 252 reels | Four batches of seven reels, 30 minutes each |
| B QA and rights cross-check | 24 reels/day | 10 | 240 reels | Full reel check and register match |

These are planning rates, not guarantees. The first week of each scanning block validates them; if throughput is lower, the contingency and the prioritisation rules in section 8 apply.

### 4.5 Quality and publication standard

- **Collection A:** 400 ppi, 24-bit colour TIFF masters; JPEG access copies; no OCR (the registers are handwritten); collection-level and item-level metadata derived from the scanning manifest.
- **Collection B:** 2K scan, 16-bit DPX or 10-bit ProRes masters; H.264 access copies; frame-level checks; audio captured where present.
- **All outputs:** SHA-256 checksums at capture, on transfer and before publication; 3-2-1 backup (master at CRO, encrypted drive copy, offline copy); persistent identifiers and stable URLs.
- **Publication:** CRO catalogue and publication server; clear rights statements; Collection B carries an orphan-works notice and a take-down contact; Collection A is marked public domain.
- **Accessibility:** catalogue descriptions and captions where feasible; alt text for representative images.

These are programme standards. They should be checked against the Partnership’s digital preservation policy before the first ingest.

---

## 5. Month-by-month schedule, January–June 2026

| Month | Collection A | Collection B | Collection C, rights and governance | Gate / milestone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **January** | Conservation starts **Mon 5 Jan** (20 of 30 days); triage all 1,800 volumes; stable-first queue; Bindwell contract; scanner setup plan. | Rights assessment **12–30 Jan** (15 days); reel inventory and condition check in the cold store; Northgate site survey; Filmtek booking; encrypted-drive test. | Written permission request to the Harrow estate; funder clarification of the rights-assessment wording; board baseline; monthly report. | **Fri 30 Jan — Gate 1:** rights assessment complete; conservation on track; Northgate and Filmtek readiness signed off; contracts in place. |
| **February** | Scanning **2–27 Feb** (20 days; 1,500 volumes); conservation completes **Fri 13 Feb**; the 220 stabilised volumes are released and queued. | Batch-protocol dry run; environmental baseline; scanner delivery and installation plan; rights-register QA. | No C spend; monthly permission follow-up; board review of A throughput. | **Fri 27 Feb — Gate 2:** 1,500 A volumes scanned; 220 volumes stabilised; Northgate dry run passed; Filmtek on track for 9 March. |
| **March** | Scanning **2–6 Mar** (5 days; 375 volumes of capacity); A scanning complete by **Fri 6 Mar**; QA and ingest start **23 Mar**. | Filmtek on site **9–20 Mar**; 240 reels scanned at 28/day; daily fixity and encrypted transfer; cold-store return after every batch. | Rights register cross-checked against scanned reels; C monthly letter; board review of nitrate batch logs. | **Fri 20 Mar — Gate 3:** all 240 reels scanned; environmental log compliant; A scanning complete; chain of custody complete. |
| **April** | QA and ingest **23 Mar – 10 Apr**; first publication tranche **30 Apr**. | QA and rights sign-off **13–24 Apr**; Collection B published **30 Apr**. | No C spend; board review of permission status; funder progress report. | **Thu 30 Apr — Gate 4:** B published; A QA complete; first A tranche live. |
| **May** | Full A publication **22 May**; final QA and fixity check. | Post-publication monitoring; take-down process; evaluation data. | Newsletter using the **2,340** visitor figure; funder report draft. | **Fri 29 May — Gate 5:** A and B fully digitised and published; internal deadline met. |
| **June** | No new scanning; fixity re-check; handover to collections team. | No new scanning; final rights and access review. | Final report, finance reconciliation, lessons learned; C status recorded. | **Tue 30 Jun — Gate 6:** grant condition evidenced; spend at or below £84,000; final report submitted. |

**Critical path:** A conservation (5 Jan – 13 Feb) → A scanning (2 Feb – 6 Mar) → A QA (23 Mar – 10 Apr) → A publication (30 Apr / 22 May). Collection B is a parallel track: rights assessment (12–30 Jan) → Filmtek (9–20 Mar) → QA (13–24 Apr) → publication (30 Apr). The two scanning blocks do not overlap, which is deliberate: one digital archivist cannot supervise CRO and Northgate at the same time, and nitrate work needs uninterrupted environmental attention.

**Schedule float:** both collections are published by 29 May, leaving June for compliance evidence, final reporting and any repair work. The internal deadline is the risk control, not the grant deadline.

---

## 6. Budget

### 6.1 Line-item budget

All figures are in pounds sterling. Staff rates are fully loaded planning rates (salary plus on-costs, or contractor equivalent). Vendor rates are those quoted in `sources/vendors.md`.

| Ref | Line item | Basis | Unit cost | Total | Spend month(s) |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | Filmtek nitrate scanner hire | Two-week booking, 10 working days (1 install/calibration + 9 scanning) | £1,200/day | £12,000 | March |
| 2 | Filmtek transport | Two journeys | £1,800 each way | £3,600 | March |
| 3 | Bindwell book-cradle scanner | 26 days (25 scanning + 1 setup/buffer) | £700/day | £18,200 | February–March |
| 4 | Conservation stabilisation, Collection A | 220 volumes, 30 working days, including materials | £300/day | £9,000 | January–February |
| 5 | Rights risk assessment, Collection B | 15 staff days (three weeks), per-reel register | £260/day | £3,900 | January |
| 6 | Encrypted drives | Four drives for capture, transfer and backup | £300 each | £1,200 | January and March |
| 7 | Publication and access hosting | Access copies, catalogue ingest, hosting configuration | 1 lot | £1,200 | April–May |
| 8 | Programme manager | 39 days across six months (0.3 FTE) | £320/day | £12,480 | January–June |
| 9 | Digital archivist | 52 days across six months (0.4 FTE) | £250/day | £13,000 | January–June |
| 10 | Metadata and publications officer | 26 days across six months (0.2 FTE) | £200/day | £5,200 | January–June |
|  | **Committed subtotal** |  |  | **£79,780** |  |
| 11 | **Contingency** | 5.0% of grant; held centrally |  | **£4,220** | Released by board approval |
|  | **Total** |  |  | **£84,000** |  |

### 6.2 Monthly cashflow

| Line | Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr | May | Jun | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Filmtek hire | 0 | 0 | 12,000 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 12,000 |
| Filmtek transport | 0 | 0 | 3,600 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 3,600 |
| Bindwell | 0 | 14,000 | 4,200 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 18,200 |
| Conservation | 6,000 | 3,000 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 9,000 |
| Rights assessment | 3,900 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 3,900 |
| Encrypted drives | 900 | 0 | 300 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1,200 |
| Publication/hosting | 0 | 0 | 0 | 600 | 600 | 0 | 1,200 |
| Programme manager | 2,080 | 2,080 | 2,080 | 2,080 | 2,080 | 2,080 | 12,480 |
| Digital archivist | 2,000 | 2,250 | 3,000 | 2,500 | 2,000 | 1,250 | 13,000 |
| Metadata officer | 800 | 800 | 800 | 1,200 | 1,200 | 400 | 5,200 |
| **Committed spend** | **15,680** | **22,130** | **25,980** | **6,380** | **5,880** | **3,730** | **79,780** |
| Contingency (held) |  |  |  |  |  |  | **4,220** |
| **Total** |  |  |  |  |  |  | **84,000** |

The profile is front-loaded because conservation, scanning and the Filmtek fortnight fall in the first quarter. The Partnership should confirm that its working-capital arrangements can carry the February–March peak if grant payments are made in arrears.

### 6.3 Budget notes and assumptions

- **Filmtek booking:** the two-week minimum is treated as 10 working days, not 14 calendar days. Day one is installation and calibration; nine days are scanning. This is the single most important commercial assumption to confirm before the purchase order.
- **Bindwell:** 26 days at the quoted day rate. The scanner is on site from 1 February; the contract must reserve the two blocks around the Filmtek fortnight.
- **Conservation:** the rate includes labour and stabilisation materials. If the conservator finds more than 220 volumes needing work, additional days come from contingency and the queue is re-prioritised; the 1,580 stable volumes are not held up.
- **Rights assessment:** 15 staff days is the whole-collection estimate, with a documented record for each of the 240 reels. It is not 15 days per reel; that reading would require 720 weeks and is not a deliverable within any realistic grant.
- **Staff:** the grant-funded team is coordination, supervision, QA and publication. The Partnership provides imaging technicians, the CRO imaging suite, the Northgate cold store and inspection room, the publication server, finance and HR support in kind. These in-kind contributions are not valued in the £84,000 and should be recorded as match funding if the application requires it.
- **VAT:** the budget assumes vendor rates are inclusive of VAT or that VAT is recoverable. Finance should confirm the treatment before contracts are signed; an irrecoverable VAT liability would need to be met from contingency.
- **No Collection C costs:** there is no C digitisation, treatment or publication line. This is deliberate and is the main reason the A+B programme fits comfortably within the grant.

### 6.4 Contingency and change control

The £4,220 contingency is 5.0% of the grant. It is held centrally and released only by the Programme Board, in this order of priority:

1. Additional Filmtek days if nitrate throughput falls below 28 reels/day.
2. Additional conservation days if more than 220 A volumes need stabilisation.
3. Additional Bindwell days if A throughput falls below 75 volumes/day.
4. Additional QA/publication days if ingest slips.

It is **not** available for Collection C. Any C work would require written permission and a funder-approved variation, not a quiet reallocation.

Any change over £1,000 or five working days requires a written change request and board approval. Any change to the grant-funded scope requires funder approval.

### 6.5 Value for money

- **Bindwell versus MobileScan:** for 26 days, Bindwell costs £18,200. MobileScan would cost £24,700 in day rates plus £2,700 in item charges for 1,800 volumes — £27,400 — and it handles paper only, not bound volumes. Bindwell is both cheaper and technically required for the book cradle.
- **Filmtek:** the two-week minimum is the only nitrate-capable option in the pack. The plan uses 252 reels of capacity for 240 reels, a 5% margin, rather than paying for a third week.
- **Conservation:** stabilising 220 volumes prevents damage to fragile bindings and avoids re-scanning or conservation treatment after the programme. It is 10.7% of the budget and protects 100% of Collection A.
- **Rights assessment:** at 4.6% of the budget, it unlocks publication of all 240 reels and is a grant condition. Without it, Collection B cannot be published at all.
- **Contingency:** 5.0% is deliberately modest but sufficient to cover the most likely overruns — a few extra scanner days or conservation days. It is cheaper than over-booking vendors in the baseline.

---

## 7. Why this plan: decision log

| # | Decision | Rationale | Trade-off accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Deliver A and B in full; do not commit to C.** | C’s written permission is unlikely before autumn 2026, and 950 boxes plus mould treatment cannot be delivered in the remaining weeks. A and B are the only pair that can satisfy the two-collection condition. | C remains undigitised in this phase. The permission request is kept alive, and any permission becomes a future project or a funder variation. |
| 2 | **Scan B at the Northgate inspection room, not CRO.** | 16°C and 45% RH are inside Filmtek’s operating range; the cold store is 4°C; CRO is not certified for film and failed the 2024 pilot at 62% RH. | No network at Northgate, so encrypted drives and a daily courier; strict 30-minute batch discipline. |
| 3 | **Schedule B for 9–20 March, after A scanning.** | Avoids summer humidity; allows the rights assessment and site preparation to finish; prevents one archivist supervising two sites at once. | A must be finished by 6 March. The 26 Bindwell days and the stable-first queue create that buffer. |
| 4 | **Stabilise 220 A volumes but scan the stable volumes first.** | Conservation takes six weeks; waiting would consume almost half the programme. Stable-first keeps the scanner productive without risking brittle bindings. | More complex queue management; the conservator must sign off each batch before scanning. |
| 5 | **Use Bindwell, not MobileScan, for A.** | A book cradle is required for brittle bound volumes. Bindwell is £700/day; MobileScan is £950/day plus £1.50/item and handles paper only. | Bindwell is available from 1 February and only “when not in use”; the contract must reserve the days in January. |
| 6 | **Book Filmtek for the two-week minimum and plan 28 reels/day.** | The 30-minute window, not the 40-reel cap, is the binding constraint. Four batches of seven reels give 28/day and 252 reels of capacity over nine scanning days. | Little slack for unusually long reels; a commissioning test and contingency days are essential. |
| 7 | **Complete the B rights assessment before publication, with a per-reel register.** | It is a grant condition. Fifteen staff days is the three-week estimate in the pack; a per-reel record makes the assessment auditable. | The pack’s wording is ambiguous. If the funder meant three weeks per reel, B is undeliverable and a variation would be needed; this is confirmed in January. |
| 8 | **Set an internal publication deadline of 29 May.** | A one-month buffer protects against QA, ingest or metadata slippage and leaves June for compliance and reporting. | A’s publication is compressed into May; batch publication and metadata templates are needed. |
| 9 | **Hold 5% contingency and spend nothing on C.** | Nitrate throughput, environmental control and conservation overrun are the real risks. The contingency protects the two-collection condition. | Limited upside for C; any C work needs a funder variation. |
| 10 | **Use encrypted drives and a daily chain of custody for B.** | Northgate has no network, and nitrate files must be secure and auditable from capture to CRO. | Manual courier and staff time, but a clear audit trail and no network dependency. |

---

## 8. Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Trigger and owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Filmtek throughput falls below 28 reels/day because of the 30-minute window | Medium | High | Commissioning test on day one; 6–7 reel batches; four batches/day; contingency days; prioritise shorter reels if necessary | Fewer than 240 reels by 18 March — Digital Archivist |
| Northgate temperature or humidity goes outside 15–20°C / 40–50% RH | Low | High | Continuous logger; alarms at 15°C and 50% RH; abort and return reels to cold store; conservator on call; dehumidifier available | Any excursion over five minutes — Conservator / Site Manager |
| Collection A conservation overruns | Medium | Medium | Stable-first queue; additional conservator days from contingency; re-sequence the fragile volumes to the end of the scanning block | More than five days behind by 6 February — Conservator / Programme Manager |
| Bindwell unavailable or breaks down | Low | High | Contract hold for the two blocks; service-level agreement; MobileScan as a fallback for stable paper only; spare days in the scanning block | No scanner on 2 February — Programme Manager |
| Rights assessment finds high-risk or unresolved reels | Medium | Medium | Publish with a risk statement or restricted access; escalate to the funder; complete the register before 24 April | Any reel unresolved by 10 April — Rights Officer / Programme Manager |

## Appendix A — Capacity calculations

**Collection A**

- 1,800 volumes at 75 volumes/day = 24.0 scanning days.
- Scheduled: 20 days in February + 5 days in March = 25 scanning days.
- Capacity: 25 × 75 = 1,875 volumes; margin = 75 volumes (4.2%).
- Bindwell booking: 25 scanning days + 1 setup/buffer day = 26 days.
- Conservation: 220 volumes at 7.3 volumes/day = 30 working days (six weeks).

**Collection B**

- 240 reels at 28 reels/day = 8.6 scanning days; scheduled 9 days.
- Capacity: 9 × 28 = 252 reels; margin = 12 reels (5.0%).
- Batches: 240 ÷ 7 = 34.3, rounded up to 35 batches; at four batches/day = 8.75 days, rounded up to 9 days.
- Filmtek booking: 1 installation/calibration day + 9 scanning days = 10 working days.
- Rights assessment: 240 reels ÷ 15 days = 16 reels/day.

**Collection A QA**

- 1,800 volumes ÷ 15 days = 120 volumes/day.

**Collection B QA**

- 240 reels ÷ 10 days = 24 reels/day.

---

## Appendix B — Nitrate batch protocol

1. **Before the batch:** check the inspection room is within 15–20°C and 40–50% RH; record the reading; confirm the scanner is calibrated; prepare a batch list of no more than 40 reels — in practice seven.
2. **Retrieve:** move the batch through the pass-through hatch from the cold store. Start the timer when the first reel leaves the cold store.
3. **Scan:** scan the batch. The clock includes scanning time, not just handling. Target 25 minutes to leave a five-minute margin.
4. **Return:** return every reel to the cold store through the hatch. Stop the timer and record the door-to-door time. The hard limit is 30 minutes.
5. **Abort:** if temperature or humidity goes outside range, or condensation appears on any reel, stop immediately, return the batch to the cold store, quarantine the affected reels and notify the Conservator.
6. **Data:** write files to an encrypted drive, generate SHA-256 checksums, complete the chain-of-custody form and transfer to CRO the same day.
7. **Log:** record batch number, reel IDs, start and end times, environmental readings, scanner operator, conservator sign-off and any incident.

---

## Appendix C — Collection B rights assessment checklist

For every reel, record:

- Reel identifier, title or working title, date, maker and provenance.
- Rights holders identified and the sources searched (Film Society minutes, donor records, local press, Companies House, the IPO orphan works register, and any other reasonable source).
- Search date, searcher and findings.
- Risk rating and the proposed publication decision (publish, publish with notice, restrict).
- Reviewer sign-off and date.
- Any take-down or contact information.

The register is complete only when all 240 reels have a record. Publication approval requires the Rights Officer and Programme Manager to sign the register and the publication checklist. Collection B carries an orphan-works notice and a take-down contact on the public catalogue.

# Wrenfield Archive Partnership

## 2026 Digitisation Programme — Delivery Plan and Budget

**Version:** 1.0 for the January 2026 Programme Board  
**Prepared by:** Programme Planner, Wrenfield Archive Partnership  
**Grant:** Heritage Digitisation Fund, £84,000  
**Programme period:** 1 January – 30 June 2026

---

## 1. Summary

The plan delivers **Collections A and B in full** and publishes both by **Friday 29 May 2026**, one month inside the grant deadline. Collection C is **not published in this phase**: the only written legal advice says the Harrow estate is unlikely to decide before autumn 2026, and a verbal “spring” assurance cannot satisfy a donor restriction that requires written permission.

The budget is **£84,000 exactly**: £79,780 committed and £4,220 (5.0%) held as contingency. The critical path is Collection A conservation, then A scanning, then A quality assurance and publication. Collection B runs on a separate Northgate track in March, after the A scanning block and before the summer humidity that defeated the 2024 nitrate pilot.

| Collection | Items | Controlling constraint | Delivery approach | Publish by | Direct cost |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| **A — Parish registers** | 1,800 bound volumes | 220 volumes (12.2%) need stabilisation first; book cradle required | Stabilise Jan–13 Feb; scan stable volumes first; 26 Bindwell days; complete scanning 6 Mar | **22 May 2026** | £27,200 |
| **B — Wrenfield Film Society** | 240 nitrate reels | Orphan works; cold storage; Filmtek only in the Northgate inspection room; 30-minute batch limit | Rights assessment Jan; Filmtek 9–20 Mar at 28 reels/day; QA and publish April | **30 Apr 2026** | £19,500 |
| **C — Harrow Estate papers** | 950 boxes | Donor restriction to 2030; written estate permission required; 8% mould-affected | No digitisation spend or publication in this phase; written permission pursued monthly | **Not in this phase** | £0 |

Direct costs above exclude the centrally held programme staff, shared data/publication costs and contingency. The full reconciliation is in section 6.

**Bottom line:** A and B are fully digitised and published by 29 May; the grant condition is met with a month of schedule float; C is a documented, deliberate exclusion rather than an unfunded aspiration.

---

## 2. Grant conditions and how the plan meets them

| Grant condition | How this plan meets it | Evidence at 30 June 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| At least two of the three priority collections fully digitised and published by 30 June 2026 | Collection A: all 1,800 volumes scanned, quality-assured and published by 22 May. Collection B: all 240 reels scanned, rights-assessed and published by 30 April. Internal deadline 29 May. | Scanning manifests, QA sign-off, live publication URLs, board completion certificate |

The register is cross-checked against the scanned reels during April QA; publication is signed off only when every reel has a completed record. | Per-reel rights register, rights officer sign-off, publication approval minute |

Reels return to the 4°C cold store after every batch. Batches stay within the policy limit of 40 reels and 30 minutes door-to-door, including scanning. | Batch log with timestamps, environmental logger data, conservator sign-off, encrypted-drive chain-of-custody records |

## 3. The open questions: decisions and evidence

Can Northgate support scanning the nitrate collection with the Filmtek scanner, and under what conditions? | **Yes — in the Northgate inspection room, not the cold store and not CRO.** | The inspection room is 16°C and 45% RH, inside Filmtek’s 15–20°C and 40–50% RH range. The cold store is 4°C and 35% RH, too cold and dry for the scanner. CRO is not certified for film and failed the 2024 pilot when humidity reached 62% and condensation appeared on 14 frames. | Filmtek is booked at Northgate for 9–20 March. The batch protocol in Appendix B applies. Digitised files travel to CRO on encrypted drives because Northgate has no network. |

This is the Partnership’s own recorded figure. | Use “2,340 visitors” in the June newsletter and the evaluation report. No further research is required. |

Plan for no; treat any permission as upside.** | The estate’s solicitor wrote in August 2025 that a decision is unlikely before autumn 2026. ### 3.1 Question 1 in detail — the Northgate conditions

The inspection room is the only compliant location in the Partnership’s estate for the Filmtek scanner:

- **Temperature and humidity:** 16°C and 45% RH are comfortably inside the scanner’s 15–20°C and 40–50% RH operating range. The room is adjacent to the cold store and connected by a pass-through hatch, so reels do not need outdoor acclimatisation.
- **Cold store:** 4°C and 35% RH. The scanner cannot operate there, and nitrate must return to cold storage whenever it is not being scanned.
- **CRO:** certified at 18–22°C and 40–55% RH for paper, but not certified for film. The 2024 pilot is decisive evidence against repeating nitrate work there: humidity reached 62% by the afternoon, condensation appeared on 14 frames, and the conservator stopped the run. ### 3.3 Question 3 in detail — the Collection C decision

Collection C cannot be published without written permission from the Harrow estate. The evidence points in two directions:

- The estate’s solicitor wrote in **August 2025** that a decision is **unlikely before autumn 2026**.
- The donor liaison officer recorded a **verbal assurance in September 2025** that the estate “expects to resolve it by spring”.

A verbal assurance is not written permission, and it is contradicted by the solicitor’s written advice. The prudent planning assumption is that written permission will **not** arrive before 30 June 2026. Collection C is therefore excluded from the two-collection commitment. The Partnership will:

1. Send a written permission request in the first week of January, copied to the estate’s solicitor.
2. Follow up monthly and log every response.
3. Commit **no digitisation spend** to C in this grant period.
4. If written permission arrives unexpectedly, treat it as upside and seek a funder-approved variation. It will not be used to displace A or B, and 950 boxes could not be fully digitised in the remaining weeks in any case.

The 8% of C that is mould-affected (about 76 boxes) is a collections-care issue. It is flagged to the conservator and kept out of the digitisation workflow; handling mould-affected material without treatment would create a health and conservation risk.

## 4. Delivery strategy

### 4.1 Collection A — Parish registers (1,800 bound volumes)

**The constraint.** About 12% of the collection — 220 volumes, using the conservator’s estimate — has binding failure and needs stabilisation before scanning. The conservator estimates six weeks for 220 volumes. Scanning must use a book cradle, and spines must never be pressed.

**The approach.** Conservation starts on **Monday 5 January** and runs for 30 working days, finishing on **Friday 13 February**. The 1,580 volumes that do not need stabilisation are queued first, so scanning can start on **Monday 2 February** while conservation finishes the fragile 220. The conservator signs off each batch of stabilised volumes before it enters the scanning queue.

Bindwell is booked for **26 days** at CRO: 25 scanning days plus one setup/buffer day. At a planning rate of 75 volumes per day, 25 days give 1,875 volumes of capacity against 1,800 required — a 4.2% margin. The scanning block runs **2 February – 6 March**, with 20 days in February (1,500 volumes) and five days in March (375 volumes). Collection A scanning is complete by **Friday 6 March**.

Quality assurance and ingest run **23 March – 10 April**, at a planning rate of 120 volumes per day. The first publication tranche goes live on **30 April**, and the full collection is published by **Friday 22 May**.

**Why scan stable volumes first.** Waiting for all 220 volumes to be stabilised would consume six of the programme’s 26 weeks before a single image was captured. Stable-first sequencing keeps the scanner productive, protects the fragile volumes, and still leaves a month of publication float.

### 4.2 Collection B — Wrenfield Film Society (240 nitrate reels)

**The constraint.** Nitrate film must be cold-stored when not being scanned. The scanner can only operate in the Northgate inspection room, and reels can leave the cold store only in batches of up to 40 for at most 30 minutes, including scanning time. The collection is orphan works, so a documented rights risk assessment is required before publication.

**The approach.** The rights assessment runs **12–30 January** (15 staff days, the equivalent of three weeks), producing a per-reel register. The assessment has schedule float to **10 April** before the publication gate, so a slower search does not put the deadline at risk.

Filmtek is booked for the two-week minimum, **9–20 March**. Day one is installation and calibration; the remaining nine days are scanning. At four batches per day of seven reels, and 28 reels per day, nine days give **252 reels of capacity** against 240 required — a 5% margin. Each batch is timed door-to-door and returned to the cold store immediately after scanning. The environmental logger runs continuously, and the conservator can stop the run at any point.

Quality assurance and the per-reel rights cross-check run **13–24 April**. Collection B is published on **Thursday 30 April**, after the rights officer and programme manager sign off every reel.

**Why March, not summer.** The 2024 pilot failed in July at CRO when humidity reached 62%. Scheduling B in March, in the controlled Northgate inspection room, avoids both the summer risk and the CRO environmental failure. It also places B after the A scanning block, so one digital archivist is not trying to supervise two sites at once.

### 4.3 Collection C — Harrow Estate papers (950 boxes)

Collection C is **not a delivery target** in this phase. The donor restriction requires written estate permission before any publication; the written legal advice says a decision is unlikely before autumn 2026. The collection is also large (950 boxes) and 8% mould-affected, so even a late permission could not produce a full digitisation by 30 June. No C digitisation spend is committed. The permission request is kept alive, and any written permission would be handled through a funder variation rather than by silently reallocating A or B resources.

## Appendix B — Nitrate batch protocol

1. **Before the batch:** check the inspection room is within 15–20°C and 40–50% RH; record the reading; confirm the scanner is calibrated; prepare a batch list of no more than 40 reels — in practice seven.
2. **Retrieve:** move the batch through the pass-through hatch from the cold store. Start the timer when the first reel leaves the cold store.
3. **Scan:** scan the batch. The clock includes scanning time, not just handling. Target 25 minutes to leave a five-minute margin.
4. **Return:** return every reel to the cold store through the hatch. Stop the timer and record the door-to-door time. The hard limit is 30 minutes.
5. **Abort:** if temperature or humidity goes outside range, or condensation appears on any reel, stop immediately, return the batch to the cold store, quarantine the affected reels and notify the Conservator.
6. **Data:** write files to an encrypted drive, generate SHA-256 checksums, complete the chain-of-custody form and transfer to CRO the same day.
7. **Log:** record batch number, reel IDs, start and end times, environmental readings, scanner operator, conservator sign-off and any incident.

---

## Appendix C — Collection B rights assessment checklist

For every reel, record:

- Reel identifier, title or working title, date, maker and provenance.
- Rights holders identified and the sources searched (Film Society minutes, donor records, local press, Companies House, the IPO orphan works register, and any other reasonable source).
- Search date, searcher and findings.
- Risk rating and the proposed publication decision (publish, publish with notice, restrict).
- Reviewer sign-off and date.
- Any take-down or contact information.

The register is complete only when all 240 reels have a record. Publication approval requires the Rights Officer and Programme Manager to sign the register and the publication checklist. Collection B carries an orphan-works notice and a take-down contact on the public catalogue.

**What the plan does**

- **Delivers Collections A and B in full**, publishing B by 30 April and A by 22 May 2026, with an internal deadline of 29 May and June held as buffer.
